key_insight: Staged knowledge distillation turns visual quantum reinforcement learning into a compact-head problem, allowing shallow quantum-compatible policies to learn from frozen classical visual features instead of training end-to-end from pixels.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical pathway for deploying small VQC-based control heads in high-dimensional visual RL settings where direct quantum policy training is unstable or too expensive.
method: Train a classical visual teacher on pixel observations.
Freeze the teacher encoder as a fixed feature interface.
Distil teacher behavior into compact downstream heads, including angle-encoded or amplitude-encoded VQC students.
evidence_signal: The pipeline was evaluated on CartPole Pixels and Acrobot Pixels, with angle-encoded VQC heads achieving near-teacher performance and amplitude-encoded heads trading performance for extreme compactness.
watch_item: Amplitude encoding is fragile and budget-sensitive, and the VQC variants incur higher simulation time than compact classical heads.
paper_title: Staged Hybridisation for Visual Quantum Reinforcement Learning via Knowledge Distillation
